required_changes_injected: Criterion 2 (Carry-forward consistency) violation: Competition component scored 4/10 with explicit statement that prior cumulative score of 7/10 was based on 'overstated' evidence (Amplitude is analytics tool, not experimentation platform). The analysis correctly identifies this as a 'cumulative state characterization error' but then downgrades from 7/10 to 4/10. Per rubric, Identified or Partial components must remain at that level unless recent call contradicts them. The recent call does NOT contradict the competitive landscape—it reinforces the build vs. buy dynamic already known. The correction to remove Amplitude as a false competitive credit should have been a clarification note maintaining the 7/10 (or justified downgrade based on new call evidence), not a retroactive restatement. If downgrading Competition from 7/10 to 4/10, this requires explicit documentation of what in the recent call drove that revision—the analysis instead attributes it to a historical scoring error, which is a carry-forward violation. Additionally, Criterion 3 (Evidence quality): Competition section notes 'No external named competitors from GrowthBook's competitive set mentioned' — this is correct, but the 4/10 score lacks sufficient evidence to justify it above 2/10 (only 'in-house experimentation platform' qualifies). The in-house build is competition, but without direct quotes or prospect-originated competitive pressure language, evidence quality is weak for the stated score. Recommendation: Either maintain 7/10 with explicit note 'Amplitude evidence corrected as not competitive, but build vs. buy dynamic from prior calls remains; no new external competitor information in recent call,' or downgrade to 2/10 with evidence that only the homegrown build is documented and external competitors remain unstated.
